title: Sixty-two years, 24 moments
lede: From one appliance store to a chain of 228, and from a bankruptcy to a website under new owners. Filter by thread.

events.title: The first store
events.text: Henry Harold Gregg and his wife, Fansy, found the company in Indianapolis.

events.title: Private equity arrives
events.text: Freeman Spogli recapitalizes the company, putting in $111.2M of equity; about $286.4M goes to existing shareholders.

events.title: Public at $13
events.text: The IPO sells 9,375,000 shares at $13.00 on the NYSE. The company has 79 stores in eight states.

events.title: 91 stores
events.text: Fiscal 2008 ends with 91 stores, $1.26B of sales and comparable-store sales up 4.8%.

events.title: Comparable sales turn
events.text: Comparable-store sales fall 8.3% in fiscal 2009, the first of eight straight declines.

events.title: 131 stores
events.text: Fiscal 2010 ends with 131 stores and $1.53B of sales.

events.title: 173 stores
events.text: Sales pass $2B in fiscal 2011.

events.title: The peak
events.text: Fiscal 2012: $2.49B of sales, $81.4M of net income, 208 stores. Video products are 43% of sales.

events.title: 228 stores
events.text: The chain reaches 228 stores; comparable-store sales fall 8.7%.

events.title: Break-even
events.text: Net income falls to $0.2M on $2.34B of sales.

events.title: A $132.7M loss
events.text: Fiscal 2015 includes $47.9M of store impairments; comparable-store sales fall 9.2%.

events.title: Appliances first
events.text: In fiscal 2016 appliances are 53% of sales; the company loses $54.9M and has about 5,100 employees.

events.title: A bad Christmas
events.text: Holiday-quarter sales fall 23.7%; the nine-month loss is $83.9M. The chain has 220 stores.

events.title: NYSE warning
events.text: The exchange says the company’s market value and equity are below its minimum.

events.title: 88 stores to close
events.text: The board approves closing 88 stores and three distribution centres.

events.title: Trading suspended
events.text: The NYSE suspends trading and starts delisting proceedings.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: hhgregg files in the Southern District of Indiana, saying it has a term sheet with an unnamed buyer.

events.title: Liquidators on standby
events.text: A consulting agreement with Tiger Capital and Great American covers the 132 remaining stores if no bid arrives.

events.title: Liquidation begins
events.text: No going-concern buyer is found; the court approves the liquidation and the sales start.

events.title: The name for sale
events.text: Hilco Streambank is hired to sell the brand, the website and over 16 million customer files.

events.title: Sold for $400,000
events.text: Valor LLC buys the name and data at auction, outbidding Sears Holdings’ $350,000.

events.title: The website returns
events.text: hhgregg.com comes back online under Valor, selling Apple watches.

events.title: Deregistered
events.text: The old company files to end its SEC registration.

events.title: Still online
events.text: hhgregg.com trades as an online electronics shop.
